Yale Cleanroom Facilities
Integrated research infrastructure for nanoscale science and engineering
As of 2025, the Yale University Cleanroom facilities at Main Campus and West Campus have been unified under a single administration. Together, they provide a particle-controlled environment supporting micro- and nanofabrication research across disciplines such as materials science, quantum computing, biomedical and chemical engineering, and environmental science. Across both sites, researchers have access to Class 1000 and Class 100 cleanroom environments, a wide range of specialized fabrication and metrology tools, and expert staff who offer equipment training and technical support.
Main Campus Cleanroom
Located in Becton Center, the Main Campus Cleanroom supports advanced micro- and nanofabrication with equipment organized into key process categories: deposition, etching, lithography, metrology, and wet processing. A dedicated Teaching Cleanroom also supports hands-on instruction. The facility is designed to accommodate diverse research needs through well-maintained infrastructure and expert technical support.
West Campus Cleanroom
Housed in Building 750, the West Campus Cleanroom includes Class 1000 wet and dry lab environments, featuring hoods for acid, base, and resist processes, as well as integrated spin coaters, hotplates, and photolithography tools. A 2020 expansion added new capabilities, including an electron beam evaporator and a reactive ion etcher. The facility is used by researchers across Yale and includes support spaces such as a gowning area, staff office, conference room, and shared workstations.

Policies
Equipment policies
Precious metals
Purchase of precious metals (e.g., gold, platinum, and palladium) is the responsibility of the research group. It is not supplied by the cleanroom.
Access and use policies
A detailed list of policies is included in the Cleanroom User Handbook.
New chemicals
Any user wishing to introduce chemicals to the cleanroom must first present an SDS to a staff member for evaluation and display an active knowledge of the chemical hazards. Approved chemicals may be brought into the cleanroom by staff members only.
Visitor access
Anyone not qualified to enter the cleanroom is considered a visitor. Upon the approval of cleanroom staff, a qualified cleanroom user may act as a host to bring a visitor in for the purpose of observation only.
After hours
The cleanroom operates Monday through Friday, 8 AM to 5 PM. All other times are considered after hours and are restricted to users with over thirty hours of Cleanroom time logged with no safety incidents.
External customers
An external customer is any non-Yale researcher who has obtained the approval of the School of Engineering & Applied Science Business Office.
Undergraduates
Undergraduate access is granted on a case-by-case basis and must be under the supervision of a senior researcher or instructor when working in the Cleanroom.
Discipline
Instances of user misconduct are evaluated and dealt with on a case-by-case basis. Consequences range from a warning and notice delivered to your PI, to permanent suspension of cleanroom access.

Cap policy
Starting in FY26, the Cleanroom and YINQE facilities have transitioned from a soft cap to a hard cap model, based on recommendations from the faculty advisory committee.
This change applies to the University Cleanroom (Becton only) and YINQE.
FY26 and Later (Hard Cap Model)
Cleanroom group cap: $50,000
YINQE group cap: $20,000
Once a group reaches its cap, a 100% discount is applied for all subsequent instrument usage for the remainder of the fiscal year.
Due to billing system limitations, the hard cap is applied as follows:
At the end of each monthly billing cycle, groups that have reached the cap are identified.
The date when the cap was exceeded is determined, and a 100% discount is applied to all sessions starting the following day through the end of the fiscal year.
The cap applies only to instrument usage; consumables and supplies continue to be charged separately.
Because of this logic, the actual total usage amount before the discount takes effect may vary slightly above the nominal cap.
Going forward, the cap levels, hourly rates, and central subsidy will be reviewed and adjusted annually to reflect changes in facility usage and operating expenses.
FY24 – FY25 (Soft Cap Model)
Cleanroom group cap: $50,000
YINQE group cap: $20,000
An 80% discount was applied to usage exceeding the cap.
The usage calculation reset at the beginning of each fiscal year.
Operating expenses for the cleanroom are recovered through the combination of hourly charges to the user community and subsidies from Yale University. All access is tracked through the Facility Online Manager (FOM) (requires Yale network access).
Instruments/equipment
Back-end processing
The cleanroom offers tools for the back-end processing of device fabrication, including a critical-point dryer and scribing and dicing tools, as well as lapping and polishing tools.
 Available to Yale researchers & external researchers
Chemical vapor deposition
The chemical vapor deposition (CVD) tools can deposit metal, oxide, and nitride thin films. The cleanroom offers various CVD tools, including plasma-enhanced CVD and atomic layer deposition.
 Available to Yale researchers & external researchers
Dry and plasma etching
Dry and plasma etching tools provide the capability to etch metals, semiconductors, and organic films at controllable rates with high selectivity.
 Available to Yale researchers & external researchers
Lithography
The cleanroom offers tools that provide a comprehensive solution for photolithography.
 Available to Yale researchers & external researchers
Metrology
Metrology tools offer the ability to characterize thin films, including via an optical microscope, spectral reflectometry, ellipsometry, stylus profiler, and optical profilometer.
 Available to Yale researchers & external researchers
Sputtering and evaporation
Physical vapor deposition (PVD) tools are used to deposit metal/oxide films under HV/UHV. This includes e-beam and thermal evaporators, plus magnetron sputtering.
 Available to Yale researchers & external researchers
Teaching cleanroom
The teaching cleanroom is located in Becton 400.
 Available to Yale researchers & external researchers
Wet benches
The cleanroom houses bench fume hoods that are dedicated to acid use, base use, solvent use, and the RCA cleaning process.

Acknowledging the cleanroom
For publications, recognition of support from the Yale Cleanroom Facilities as well as individual staff contributions may be formatted as follows:
Acknowledgment: This work was made possible by the West Campus Cleanroom, a core facility supported by the Office of the Provost of Yale University.
We’d like to thank [staff member] for [service or other contribution].
